title: Automated quantization accuracy validation harness for FP8/INT8 profiles
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: We need an automated, repeatable harness to validate accuracy when we create new quantization profiles (FP8 and INT8). Current manual QA is slow and misses edge cases (KV-cache interactions, long-context drift, structured outputs). Goal is to gate rollouts of quantized model variants via objective pass/fail checks run in CI and before canary traffic.

Success criteria / Acceptance:
- A harness that runs on CI and on release pipelines producing a concise report (HTML + JSON) per profile.
- Gates: pass if all metrics are within thresholds vs float32 baseline on the same seed set:
  * Golden prompt generation: top-1 token overlap loss <= 1.0% relative drop
  * Embedding similarity (cosine) across 10k pairs >= 0.995 average
  * Mean token KL divergence <= 0.02
  * Instruction-following rubric score delta <= 1.5 points (0-100 scale)
  * Hallucination indicator: proportion of hallucinated facts <= baseline + 0.5%
- Harness persists artifacts: per-layer activation histograms, calibration scalars, and diff heatmaps for debugging.
- Automatic gating: failed profile blocks rollout and opens ENG rollback ticket; passing profile triggers canary plan generation.

Calibration workflow (high level):
1) Select calibration dataset: 50k examples stratified across document types (conversational, instruction, code, long-form).
2) Warm-up pass to collect activations and KV-cache stats (N=3 seeds).
3) Build per-tensor and per-channel histograms using 2048-bin accumulators and compute percentile clipping candidates (99.999th, 99.99th, 99.9th).
4) Evaluate candidate scale choices using MSE and KL on a held-out calibration split; prefer symmetric per-channel for INT8, grouped per-tensor scaling for FP8 when needed.
5) Output calibration artifact (calibration.json) with chosen scalars and recommended kernel flags.
6) Re-run full validation harness against baseline to compute metrics and generate pass/fail verdict.

Implementation notes / decisions:
- INT8 path will default to per-channel symmetric quantization with dynamic zero-point where hardware requires it. FP8 path uses shared exponent tuning plus bias compensation; early experiments show FP8 retains more distribution shape but requires careful exponent bias handling.
- Store both emulated-quant results (software quantizer) and hardware-accelerated runs when available; compare both and alert if divergence > threshold (0.3% accuracy).
- KV-cache behavior: include explicit test cases (long contexts, repeated prefixes) because prefix caching interacts with quant rounding.
- Tokenizer and sampling determinism: harness pins RNG seeds and sampling temperature for generation tasks to make diffs stable.

Validation metrics & artifacts:
- Generation diffs: token-level diff heatmaps, BLEU/ROUGE-like overlap, and per-prompt pairwise exact-match rate.
- Embedding metrics: cosine distribution plots and percentile deltas.
- Instruction score: human-labeled small rubric (100 samples) + automated proxy (instruction-following classifier).
- Calibration artifacts: activation histograms, scale tables, bias adjustments.
- Performance counters: latency, peak memory, and quantization overheads per kernel.

Pass/fail gates and rollout strategy:
- Hard blocks on CI if any primary gate fails.
- If marginal fail within small amount (e.g., top-1 drop between 1.0% and 1.5%), create canary run with 1% traffic to monitor real-world metrics for 24h before blocking.
- Automatic fallback: runtime will route requests to float model when the model returns a high-uncertainty score or if runtime-level safety checks fail.

Progress / recent updates:
- 2026-02-22: Spike completed (Miguel) — prototype harness that runs generation + embedding diffs locally. Observed INT8 median cosine 0.997 vs baseline, FP8 0.999 on small 5k set.
- 2026-03-02: Design doc posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/Quantization-Validation-Harness-v1 (attachment below).
- 2026-03-05: PR created for core harness framework: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/482 (attachment). Running CI on small runner instance.
- 2026-03-09: Calibration experiments (per-channel vs per-tensor) added. INT8 per-channel yields 0.8% generation top-1 drop on a stress set; improved with 99.99th percentile clipping.
- 2026-03-12: Added KV-cache golden prompt set (1.2k prompts) and synthetic long-context tests. First full-run shows INT8 passes gates but FP8 has a small regression on code-generation samples.

Open tasks / next steps:
- Expand golden prompt corpus to 20k with more enterprise-like prompts (finance/legal) — assigned to data team (follow-up ticket).
- Integrate hardware-run comparison stage (NVIDIA A100 + Habana) into CI cluster.
- Implement automatic rollback ticket generation and canary plan templating.
- Add visual diff UI to Console (small UX spike, coordinate with PM/Design).

Acceptance criteria (explicit):
- CI job returns JSON verdict and stores artifacts to S3 per-run with signed links.
- For three representative models (gpt-lite-7b, rwd-medium-13b, rwd-large-70b), at least two quant profiles (INT8, FP8) can run through harness end-to-end and produce pass/fail reports.
- Rollout gating integrated with runtime routing rules (blocking policy + canary templating).

Notes and trade-offs:
- Strict numeric thresholds reduce false positives but may increase blocked rollouts. We prefer conservative thresholds for enterprise customers.
- FP8 gives better accuracy but is less widely supported on partner hardware; harness must show both emulation and hardware results.
